privacy_intro: This Privacy Policy explains what information PeerPilot collects, how we use it, and the choices you have, as a learner, evaluator, or institution using our peer-evaluation platform.
privacy_section_1_body: We collect the information you provide directly, such as your name, email address, and profile details, as well as the content you submit for evaluation, the evaluations you give and receive, and basic usage data like login times and device information.
privacy_section_2_body: We use your information to operate the platform: matching submissions with evaluators, calculating scores, tracking progress against thresholds, securing your account, and improving the reliability of the peer-review process.
privacy_section_3_body: Because PeerPilot is built around peer review, some of your activity is necessarily visible to others. Your submissions are shared with assigned evaluators, and your evaluations (including written feedback) are shared with the person you reviewed. Institutions you belong to can see aggregated progress and scores for oversight purposes.
privacy_section_4_body: We do not sell your personal information. We only share data with the institution you are enrolled in, service providers who help us run the platform (such as hosting and authentication providers), and authorities when required by law.
privacy_section_5_body: We retain your account and academic activity data for as long as your account is active, and for a reasonable period afterward to comply with legal obligations and resolve disputes about evaluations or scores.
privacy_section_6_body: We use local storage to remember your session, your language preference, and other settings that make the platform easier to use. We do not use third-party advertising cookies.
privacy_section_7_body: You can access, correct, or request deletion of your personal information at any time by contacting us or your institution administrator. Some academic records may need to be retained even after a deletion request, where required for institutional or legal reasons.
privacy_section_8_body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. If we make material changes, we will notify you through the platform or by email before the changes take effect.
privacy_section_9_body: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or how your data is handled, please contact your institution administrator or reach out to our support team.
terms_intro: These Terms of Service govern your use of PeerPilot, a peer-evaluation learning platform. By creating an account or using the platform, you agree to these terms.
terms_section_1_body: By accessing or using PeerPilot, you confirm that you have read, understood, and agree to be bound by these Terms of Service and our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the platform.
terms_section_2_body: PeerPilot lets students submit work, evaluate their peers, and advance based on scores validated by other learners rather than top-down grading. Institutions can configure courses, assignments, and passing thresholds for their cohorts.
terms_section_3_body: You must provide accurate information when creating an account and keep your credentials secure. You are responsible for all activity that happens under your account. Accounts are typically issued or approved by your institution.
terms_section_4_body: Evaluations must be given honestly and in good faith, based on the submitted work and the assignment's rubric. Retaliatory, biased, or collusive scoring is prohibited and may result in loss of evaluation privileges or account suspension.
terms_section_5_body: You retain ownership of the work you submit. By submitting content, you grant PeerPilot and your institution a limited license to store, display, and distribute it to assigned evaluators and staff solely for the purpose of evaluation and academic record-keeping.
terms_section_6_body: Institutions are responsible for the programmes, rubrics, and thresholds they configure, and for managing the students and staff they enroll. Institution administrators may access aggregated and individual progress data for oversight purposes.
terms_section_7_body: We may suspend or terminate access to the platform for accounts that violate these terms, including evaluation misconduct, abuse, or unauthorized access. Institutions may also remove students or staff from their organization at any time.
terms_section_8_body: PeerPilot is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind. We do not guarantee that scores, evaluations, or platform availability will be error-free or uninterrupted. To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential damages arising from your use of the platform.
terms_section_9_body: These Terms are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which PeerPilot operates, without regard to conflict-of-law principles, unless otherwise required by applicable local regulations.
terms_section_10_body: We may update these Terms from time to time. Continued use of the platform after changes take effect constitutes acceptance of the revised Terms.
terms_section_11_body: If you have questions about these Terms of Service, please contact your institution administrator or reach out to our support team.
hero_sub: Submit your work. Evaluate your peers. Advance only when others validate your effort. No grades from above — your score comes from the people learning beside you, across every field and every campus.
how_sub: Every submission requires three validated peer reviews before it counts. Your evaluators are fellow students tackling the same challenges — in medicine, design, law, or code. The discipline changes. The process doesn't. The network is the curriculum.
eval_sub: Whether it's an architectural proposal, a legal brief, or a product prototype — every piece of work gets the same rigorous, structured peer review.
eval_feedback_1: Strong spatial analysis. The zoning rationale is well-argued. Sustainability section could go deeper on long-term impact modelling.
eval_feedback_2: Compelling proposal. Visual presentation is clear. The traffic flow diagrams are a highlight — exactly what the rubric asks for.
eval_feedback_3: Meets all base criteria. Community engagement strategy is underdeveloped compared to the rest of the submission.
feature_1_desc: Submit essays, code, design files, case studies, lab reports, or presentations. Bonus scoring rewards work that exceeds the brief.
feature_2_desc: Reviewer quality is tracked. Evaluators who score unfairly or inconsistently lose review privileges — protecting every submission.
feature_3_desc: Each institution sets its own passing bar. Students advance on merit, at their own pace, with no arbitrary deadlines.
feature_4_desc: Form ad-hoc teams for collaborative work. Shared submissions with individual reviewer feedback for every contributor.
feature_5_desc: Schools and universities define programmes, set thresholds, and monitor entire cohorts from a single dashboard. No grading. Pure oversight.
feature_6_desc: Every score, every reviewer, every assignment — fully visible on the student's profile. No hidden rubrics. No surprises.
institutes_sub: PeerPilot gives institutions a lightweight layer of control without turning administrators into graders. Define your programmes, assign thresholds, and let peer evaluation do the heavy lifting — at any scale, across any discipline.
institutes_step_1: Create your institution and invite students — no per-seat pricing, no vendor lock-in.
institutes_step_2: Build courses with your own rubrics, passing thresholds, and submission formats.
institutes_step_3: Monitor cohort progress in real time. Flag outliers. Intervene only when it matters.
cta_sub: For students who want to grow through honest feedback. For institutions that trust their learners to lead the process.
